title: Bhikkhus, then the Bodhisatta Vipassī reflected: 'This consciousness turns back and forth, it does not go beyond name-and-form. Only to this extent one is born,…
content: Bhikkhus, then the Bodhisatta Vipassī reflected: 'This consciousness turns back and forth, it does not go beyond name-and-form. Only to this extent one is born, or becomes old, or dies, or passes away, or is reborn, that is: conditioned by name-and-form, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, name-and-form arises; conditioned by name-and-form, the six sense bases arise; conditioned by the six sense bases, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, craving arises; conditioned by craving, clinging arises; conditioned by clinging, existence arises; conditioned by existence, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise. Thus is the origination of this whole mass of suffering.'

title: - Bhikkhus, there are these five kinds of stinginess. What five? Stinginess regarding dwellings, stinginess regarding families, stinginess regarding gains, stinginess regarding beauty, stinginess regarding…
content: - Bhikkhus, there are these five kinds of stinginess. What five? Stinginess regarding dwellings, stinginess regarding families, stinginess regarding gains, stinginess regarding beauty, stinginess regarding Dhamma. Bhikkhus, for the abandonment of these five kinds of stinginess, the four establishments of mindfulness should be developed. What four? ... these four establishments of mindfulness should be developed.

title: Bhikkhus, when dwelling thus with mindfulness established, the bhikkhu reflects on, examines, and investigates that Dhamma with wisdom, at that time the investigation-of-states enlightenment factor…
content: Bhikkhus, when dwelling thus with mindfulness established, the bhikkhu reflects on, examines, and investigates that Dhamma with wisdom, at that time the investigation-of-states enlightenment factor is aroused in the bhikkhu. At that time, he develops the investigation-of-states enlightenment factor. At that time, the investigation-of-states enlightenment factor comes to fulfillment by development. When he reflects on, examines, and investigates that Dhamma with wisdom, unflagging energy is aroused in the bhikkhu. Bhikkhus, when the bhikkhu reflects on, examines, and investigates that Dhamma with wisdom, at that time unflagging energy is aroused in that bhikkhu. At that time, the energy enlightenment factor is aroused in the bhikkhu. At that time, he develops the energy enlightenment factor. At that time, the energy enlightenment factor comes to fulfillment by development. Non-material rapture arises in one who is energetic and striving.

title: Poverty and indebtedness Are called suffering in the world! A poor person in debt, Enjoying, is harmed, Then pursued by creditors, Even to being bound.…
content:
Poverty and indebtedness
Are called suffering in the world!
A poor person in debt,
Enjoying, is harmed,

Then pursued by creditors,
Even to being bound.
Being bound is indeed suffering
For one seeking sensual pleasures.

So too in the Noble Discipline,
Whoever lives without faith,
Without shame, without dread,
Decides on evil deeds.

Having done evil deeds
By body, speech, and mind,
And wishes: 'May no one know what I did.'

That person well conceals
With body, speech, and mind,
Increases evil deeds,
Here and there doing more.

An evil-witted, evil-deed person,
Knowing the evil he has done,
Like a poor person in debt,
Enjoying, is harmed.

Painful thoughts
Born from remorse
Still pursue that person,
In the village or in the forest.

An evil-deed, evil-witted person,
Knowing the evil he has done,
Either falls into the animal realm
Or is bound in hell.

This binding is suffering.
The wise are liberated.
One with serene mind who gives
With righteously gained goods,

Sowing good fortune on both paths,
A faithful householder seeking,
In the present obtains happiness,
In the hereafter obtains bliss.
Thus a householder's giving
Increases merit.

So too in the Noble Discipline
Faith is established.
With shame, with dread,
With wisdom, protecting virtue,

That one, in the Noble Discipline,
Is called 'one who dwells happily.'
He gains non-material happiness,
Established in equanimity.

Abandoning the five hindrances,
Always diligent, energetic,
Attains jhāna, one-pointed mind,
Careful, mindful.

Knowing that as it really is,
He destroys all fetters,
Without any clinging,
Rightly, his mind is liberated.

With that right liberation,
If such knowledge arises:
'Unshakable is my liberation,
The fetter of existence is destroyed.'

This knowledge is supreme knowledge,
This happiness is unsurpassed happiness,
Without sorrow, without defilement,
Secure, liberated.
This state of being free from debt
Is considered the highest.

title: Just as, Sunakkhatta, a person who has not been living in his own village or town for a long time might see a person who…
content: Just as, Sunakkhatta, a person who has not been living in his own village or town for a long time might see a person who has just arrived from that village or town. He would ask that person about the safety of that village or town, about the abundance of food and drink, and about the absence of disease; and that person would tell him about the safety, abundance, and good health. Sunakkhatta, what do you think? Would that person listen to him, lend an ear, and fix his mind on that knowledge, and would he associate with that person with delight?" — "Yes, Venerable Sir." — "So too, Sunakkhatta, this situation occurs when some people are heavily inclined towards material things. For one heavily inclined towards material things, Sunakkhatta, a talk that is suitable for him must be in accordance with his reflections and thoughts, and he will only associate with that person with delight. But if the talk is only about the imperturbable (āneñja), he will not listen, will not lend an ear, will not fix his mind on supreme knowledge, and will not associate with that person with delight. He should be understood as: 'A person heavily inclined towards material things.'

title: Bhikkhus, just as a great tree, all its roots going downward and spreading out, bring sap to the tree. Bhikkhus, that great tree, being nourished,…
content: Bhikkhus, just as a great tree, all its roots going downward and spreading out, bring sap to the tree. Bhikkhus, that great tree, being nourished, being supplied, would stand for a long time. So too, bhikkhus, one who lives seeing gratification in things that can be clung to, craving increases. With craving as condition, clinging arises ... Thus is the origination of this whole mass of suffering. Bhikkhus, just as a great tree, a man comes with a shovel and a basket. He cuts the tree's roots ... or lets the ashes be carried away by a swift stream. Thus, bhikkhus, that great tree has its roots cut, made like a palm stump, made not to arise again, unable to live again in the future. So too, bhikkhus, one who lives seeing danger in things that can be clung to, craving ceases. With the cessation of craving, clinging ceases ... Thus is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.

title: Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and abides in the first jhāna ... the second jhāna ... the…
content: Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and abides in the first jhāna ... the second jhāna ... the third jhāna ... enters and abides in the fourth jhāna. This is called the pleasure of renunciation, the pleasure of seclusion, the pleasure of peace, the pleasure of enlightenment. 'I say that this kind of pleasure should be pursued, should be developed, should be cultivated, and should not be feared.' When it is said: 'One should know the evaluation of pleasure; having evaluated pleasure, one should be intent on inner pleasure' — it was for this reason that this was said.

title: When the sun rises, bhikkhus, this is the forerunner, this is the herald, namely the dawn. So too, bhikkhus, for wholesome states, this is the…
content: When the sun rises, bhikkhus, this is the forerunner, this is the herald, namely the dawn. So too, bhikkhus, for wholesome states, this is the forerunner, this is the herald, namely right view. From right view, bhikkhus, comes right intention. From right intention comes right speech. From right speech comes right action. From right action comes right livelihood. From right livelihood comes right effort. From right effort comes right mindfulness. From right mindfulness comes right concentration. From right concentration comes right knowledge. From right knowledge comes right liberation.

title: Bhikkhus, there are these three kinds of purity. What three? Purity of body, purity of speech, and purity of mind. Bhikkhus, these are the three…
content:
Bhikkhus, there are these three kinds of purity. What three? Purity of body, purity of speech, and purity of mind. Bhikkhus, these are the three kinds of purity.

Purity of body and speech,
Purity of mind, without taints,
One who is pure, possessing purity,
Is called one who has abandoned all.

title: Just as, bhikkhus, a fisherman casts a baited hook into a deep lake. A fish, looking at the bait, swallows the hook. Thus, bhikkhus, that…
content: Just as, bhikkhus, a fisherman casts a baited hook into a deep lake. A fish, looking at the bait, swallows the hook. Thus, bhikkhus, that fish, having swallowed the fisherman's hook, falls into misfortune, into calamity, and is at the fisherman's mercy. So too, bhikkhus, there are these six hooks in the world, bringing misfortune to beings, bringing calamity to creatures. What six? Bhikkhus, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, connected with sensual desire, enticing. If a bhikkhu delights in those forms, praises them, and abides with attachment, then, bhikkhus, that bhikkhu is called one who has swallowed Māra's hook, who has fallen into misfortune, into calamity, and is at the Evil One's mercy. ... There are sounds cognizable by the ear ... odors cognizable by the nose ... tastes cognizable by the tongue ... tangibles cognizable by the body ... There are mind-objects cognizable by the mind that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, connected with sensual desire, enticing. If a bhikkhu delights in those mind-objects, praises them, and abides with attachment, then, bhikkhus, that bhikkhu is called one who has swallowed Māra's hook, who has fallen into misfortune, into calamity, and is at the Evil One's mercy.
